question: Which V2O5 film thicknesses were tested electrochemically, how many ALD cycles gave the thicker film, and did the potential shifts differ between them?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE regexp_matches(text, '(cycles|nm|thick|Cyclic|CV|voltammet|peak|shift)') ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (4,5,6) ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE regexp_matches(text, '(ALD|cycle|500|1000|40 |80 |∼40|∼80|nm)') ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, page, line_no, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (2,6) AND line_no BETWEEN 25 AND 40 OR (page=6 AND line_no BETWEEN 60 AND 100) ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, kind, page, strength, text FROM atoms WHERE regexp_matches(lower(text), '(cycles|cycle|ald cycles|40 nm|80 nm|∼40|∼80|1000|500 )') ORDER BY page, id

rendered: Electrochemical testing covered V2O5 films of ∼80 nm[1] and ∼40 nm[2] thickness. The thicker film was grown with 1000 ALD cycles[3]. The thinner film was made with 500[4] ALD cycles (see Fig. 1[5]). For the potential shifts, the text reports potential shifts of ∼40 mV[6] and states that similar shifts in values of ΔEeq(avg) were observed[7] for both thicknesses, owing to similar locked-in elastic strains. So the potential shifts did not differ meaningfully between the thicker and thinner films.
